long_biography.plain_text:
Paloma founder Donald Sussman once intended to become a doctor, but a summer placement in a medical examiner's office changed his plans. While working in finance, he completed his degree and MBA through evening study at New York University. His healthcare giving later focused on communities where he had lived and observed gaps in local services.

At Holy Cross Health in Fort Lauderdale, he watched patients coming for care and discussed the hospital's needs with its chief executive. He gave funds for new equipment and technology at its family health centre. He also supported the University of the Virgin Islands' medical-school project, whose classroom building was named for his father, William.
